note.explanation: A force can be split into perpendicular x- and y-components. If the force F makes an angle θ with the x-axis, use cosine for the x-component and sine for the y-component.
examples: For F = 200 N at 30° to the x-axis: F_x = 200 cos 30° = 173.2 N.
For the same force: F_y = 200 sin 30° = 100 N.
note.checkAnswer: F_x = F cos θ; F_y = F sin θ. For 200 N at 30°: F_x = 173.2 N and F_y = 100 N.
note.simple: Think of the force as the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle. Its horizontal part uses cosine, and its vertical part uses sine.
note.checkQuestion: A force of 10 N makes an angle of 30° with the x-axis. What are its x- and y-components?
note.title: Resolving a Force into Components
steps: Identify F and the angle θ it makes with the x-axis.
Substitute the values and calculate each component.
note.answer: The x-component is found using cosine, and the y-component is found using sine.

mcqs.stem: A force of 10 N makes an angle of 37° with the x-axis. Using cos 37° = 0.8, what is its x-component?
rationales: This is incorrect because the x-component is not 6 N for the given cosine value.
This is correct because F_x = F cos θ = 10 × 0.8 = 8 N.
This is incorrect because 10 N is the magnitude of the full force, not its x-component at 37°.
This is incorrect because the component cannot be greater than the force magnitude in this case.

mcqs.stem: A force F makes an angle θ with the x-axis. Which expression gives its y-component?
rationales: This is incorrect because F cos θ gives the x-component when θ is measured from the x-axis.
This is correct because F_y = F sin θ.
This is incorrect because tangent gives the ratio of the perpendicular to the base, not the component directly.
This is incorrect because dividing by sin θ does not give the y-component.

options: A component is the effective value of a vector in a given direction.
A component is always larger than the original vector.
A component is the angle between two vectors.
A component is the point where a vector begins.
mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes a component of a vector?
rationales: This is correct because a component gives the effective value of a vector in a chosen direction.
This is incorrect because a component is not larger than the original vector.
This is incorrect because an angle is not a vector component.
This is incorrect because the starting point of a vector is not its component.

options: F_x is always equal to F_y.
F_x and F_y point in the same direction.
mcqs.stem: What is the relationship between the rectangular components of a vector?
rationales: This is incorrect because rectangular components act along perpendicular axes.
This is correct because the x- and y-components are perpendicular to each other.
This is incorrect because their magnitudes depend on the force and its angle.
This is incorrect because the components act in different, perpendicular directions.

mcqs.stem: A 20 N force acts at 90° to the x-axis. What is its x-component?
rationales: This is correct because F_x = 20 cos 90° = 0 N.
This is incorrect because the x-component is zero when the force is perpendicular to the x-axis.
This is incorrect because 10 N is not obtained from the cosine of 90°.
This is incorrect because the whole force points along the y-axis, not the x-axis.

mcqs.stem: In a right-angled triangle, which ratio represents sin θ?
rationales: This is incorrect because base/hypotenuse represents cosine θ.
This is correct because sin θ is perpendicular/hypotenuse.
This is incorrect because it reverses the sine ratio.
This is incorrect because perpendicular/base represents tan θ.

mcqs.stem: A force F points straight along the positive y-axis. What are its rectangular components?
rationales: This is incorrect because the force has no x-direction component.
This is correct because the full force lies along the y-axis and its x-component is zero.
This is incorrect because the force is not at an angle that divides it equally between the axes.
This is incorrect because the component magnitudes cannot both equal the full force in this direction.

options: The x-component is greater than the y-component.
The y-component is greater than the x-component.
mcqs.stem: A force makes an angle of 45° with the x-axis. How do the magnitudes of its x- and y-components compare?
rationales: This is incorrect because sine and cosine have equal values at 45°.
This is incorrect because sine and cosine have equal values at 45°.
This is correct because F cos 45° = F sin 45°.
This is incorrect because a non-zero force at 45° has non-zero components.

written.text: What are rectangular components of a vector and their values?
written.finalAnswer: The rectangular components are the perpendicular x- and y-components: F_x = F cos θ and F_y = F sin θ.

explain.title: Resolution of a force
explain.body: To divide a force into its components is known as resolution of a force. The components add together to give the original force.

explain.title: What a component means
explain.body: A component of a vector is its effective value in a given direction. For example, the x-component tells how much of the vector acts along the x-axis.

explain.title: Rectangular components
explain.body: A force is often resolved into two components that are perpendicular to each other. These are called its perpendicular or rectangular components.

explain.title: The component formulae
explain.body: When a force F makes an angle θ with the x-axis, its components are F_x = F cos θ and F_y = F sin θ. Use the angle as measured from the x-axis.

mistakes: Swapping sine and cosine: when θ is measured from the x-axis, use cosine for F_x and sine for F_y.
Giving only one component when the question asks for both x- and y-components.
Leaving out units in a numerical answer.
Using a calculator in the wrong angle mode; these questions use degrees.
